items.description:
Product SKU format:
- Exactly two uppercase letters, but the letters I and O are not allowed.
- Followed by exactly three digits.
- Followed by a hyphen.
- Followed by one uppercase letter (excluding I and O) and then one digit.
The whole string must match this format.

SKU format:
- Begins with the literal prefix 'SKU-'.
- Then exactly three uppercase letters.
- Then a hyphen.
- Then exactly four digits.
- Optionally, a hyphen followed by exactly two uppercase letters (variant code).
The entire string must conform, with no other characters.

Our issue tracker uses JIRA-style ticket references. A valid reference has a project code of two to five uppercase letters, followed by a hyphen, then a ticket number that is a positive integer without leading zeros.
We use ULIDs as order identifiers. A ULID is 26 characters long and uses Crockford's Base32 alphabet: digits and uppercase letters, but the letters I, L, O and U are never used.

UUID version 4 format:
- 8 hexadecimal digits, then a hyphen.
- 4 hexadecimal digits, then a hyphen.
- The digit 4, then 3 hexadecimal digits, then a hyphen.
- One of the characters 8, 9, A, or B (case-insensitive), then 3 hexadecimal digits, then a hyphen.
- 12 hexadecimal digits.
Hexadecimal digits may be uppercase or lowercase.

Our design tool lets users paste HTML snippets. We need to check that a snippet contains at least one opening <div> tag. The tag may have attributes, including quoted values that contain > characters, and may span multiple lines. It must not be a self-closing tag (i.e., ending with '/>') or a closing tag.

The domain may have subdomains. After the domain, an optional port number between 1 and 65535 may appear. Then an optional path starting with /, an optional query string starting with ?, and an optional fragment starting with # may follow. The string must not contain spaces.

In our theme editor, users can specify CSS lengths for margins and paddings. We need to validate that the input is a valid CSS length. It can be a signed decimal number (with optional + or -) followed by a unit (px, em, rem, vh, vw, or %), or it can be the number zero without a unit. Units are case-insensitive.
